questions.enonce_markdown:
State the biological importance of:

(i) Nitrogen to plants,

(ii) Nitrogen fixation in nature. *(4, 5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Importance of nitrogen to plants.** Nitrogen is needed to make **amino acids and then proteins** (for protoplasm, enzymes, growth and repair of cells), **chlorophyll** (green colour, photosynthesis), **nucleic acids (DNA, RNA)** and some vitamins. Plants take it as **nitrates** (and ammonium salts) through the roots. A shortage causes **stunted growth and yellowing of leaves (chlorosis)**.

**(ii) Importance of nitrogen fixation in nature.** Atmospheric nitrogen (about 78 % of air) cannot be used directly by plants or animals. **Nitrogen fixation** converts it into **nitrates / ammonium compounds** that plants can absorb:
- by **nitrogen-fixing bacteria**: **Rhizobium** in the root nodules of legumes (beans, groundnut), and free-living **Azotobacter** and **Clostridium** in the soil;
- by **lightning**, which makes nitrogen oxides that are washed into the soil by rain.

It **replaces the nitrates lost** from the soil by leaching, denitrification and crop removal, so it **maintains soil fertility** and supplies nitrogen to the whole food chain (plants, then animals eating them). It keeps the nitrogen cycle going.

**(i) Photosynthesis.** Green plants (and algae) **remove carbon dioxide from the atmosphere** (or water) and, using **light energy absorbed by chlorophyll**, build it into **carbohydrates (glucose, starch)**, which are then changed to fats, proteins and other organic compounds. Carbon is therefore **transferred from the atmosphere into living organisms** (plants, then the animals that eat them). Oxygen is released.
$$6CO_2 + 6H_2O \xrightarrow{\text{light, chlorophyll}} C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2$$

**(ii) Respiration.** All living organisms (plants, animals, decomposers) **oxidise glucose** to release energy, and **return carbon dioxide to the atmosphere**. So carbon is **transferred from organic compounds back to the air** and becomes available for photosynthesis again.
$$C_6H_{12}O_6 + 6O_2 \rightarrow 6CO_2 + 6H_2O + \text{energy}$$

questions.enonce_markdown: How does deforestation affect the carbon cycle? *(5 marks)*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Deforestation is the cutting down and clearing of forests.

- **Fewer trees means less photosynthesis**, so **less carbon dioxide is removed** from the atmosphere and the carbon dioxide level **rises**.
- **Burning of the cleared wood** releases large amounts of carbon dioxide (and carbon monoxide) into the air.
- The **decay of logs and dead leaves** by bacteria and fungi (decomposers) releases carbon dioxide by their respiration.
- The **carbon stored in the wood of trees** (carbon sink) is lost, so the balance of the carbon cycle is upset.
- The increase of carbon dioxide (a greenhouse gas) causes the **greenhouse effect and global warming**; the oxygen supply also decreases and soil erosion increases.
